It is Madani according to the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah, and Makki according to the view of Ibn Masʿud, ʿAta', and Jabir.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "It was revealed at Madinah: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking﴾."

Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Muhammad ibn Nasr, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, who said: "A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Teach me (a surah), O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Recite three of the ones with the letter ra' (dhawat al-ra').' The man said: 'My age has grown old, my heart has become hard, and my tongue has become thick.' He said: 'Recite three of the ones with ha-mim (dhawat ha-mim).' He said the same as his first statement. He said: 'Recite three of the glorifying surahs (al-musabbihat).' He said the same as his first statement, and said: 'But teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a comprehensive surah.' So he taught him ﴿When the earth is shaken with its shaking﴾ until he finished it. The man said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I will not add to it.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'He has succeeded, the little man (al-Ruwayjil) has succeeded, the little man has succeeded.'"

At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ is credited with half of the Qur'an, whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ is credited with a third of the Qur'an, and whoever recites ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ is credited with a quarter of the Qur'an."

At-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Durays, Muhammad ibn Nasr, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "*When it is shaken* equals half of the Qur'an, ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an, and ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ equals a quarter of the Qur'an."

At-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib; we do not know it except through the hadith of Yaman ibn al-Mughirah."

At-Tirmidhi narrated from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man among his companions: "Have you married, so-and-so?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, and I do not have what I could marry with." He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a third of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the help of Allah comes and the victory﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Marry!"

At-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurairah: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever recites *When it is shaken* in a night, he will have the reward of half of the Qur'an.'"

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its shaking﴾, meaning when it is moved with a violent movement. The answer of the conditional is "it will relate" (tuhaddithu). The intended meaning is that it is moved at the establishment of the Hour, for it will convulse until everything upon it is shattered.

Mujahid said: It is the first blast, due to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 6–7]. The verbal noun is mentioned for emphasis, then it is attributed to the earth; it is a verbal noun attributed to its agent. The meaning: its particular shaking which it deserves and which its body and immensity require.

al-Jumhur read *zilzalaha* with a kasra on the zay, while al-Jahdari and ʿIsa read it with a fatha. Both are verbal nouns with the same meaning. It was said that the kasra form is a verbal noun and the fatha form is a noun (ism).

al-Qurtubi said: *al-zalzal* with a fatha is a verbal noun like *al-waswas* and *al-qalqal*.

﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, meaning what is within its interior of the dead and the hidden treasures. *Al-athqal* is the plural of *thiql*. Abu ʿUbaydah and al-Akhfash said: if the dead person is in the belly of the earth, he is a burden to it; and if he is above it, he is a burden upon it.

Mujahid said: "Its burdens" are its dead, which it brings forth at the second blast. It has been said that mankind and jinn are called *al-thaqalan* (the two burdens). The mention of "the earth" in the place of a pronoun is to increase emphasis.

﴿And man says: What is wrong with it?﴾, meaning each individual of mankind says: What has happened to it that it is shaken?, because of what overwhelms him of its affair and what dazzles him of its calamity. It was said that the intended "man" is the disbeliever. His saying "what is wrong with it" is a subject and predicate, and it carries the sense of wonder: i.e., what is the matter with it, or for what reason has it been shaken and brought forth its burdens?

His saying: *yawma'idhin* is a substitution (badal) for *idha*, and the governing element for both is His saying: ﴿it will relate its news﴾. It is permissible that the governing element of *idha* is omitted and the governing element of *yawma'idhin* is "it will relate." The meaning: on the day when it is shaken and brings forth, it will inform with its news and relate to them what was done upon it of good and evil, either by the tongue of its state, where it indicates that clearly, or by the tongue of speech, by Allah, glorified is He, making it speak.

It was said that this is connected to His saying: ﴿And man says: What is wrong with it?﴾, meaning: he said, "What is wrong with it," being amazed at that, ﴿it relates its news﴾. Yahya ibn Salam said: it relates its news by what it brought forth of its burdens. It was said: it relates the establishment of the Hour and that it has come and that the world has ended.

Ibn Jarir said: it makes clear its news by the quaking, the earthquake, and the bringing forth of the dead. The first object of *tuhaddithu* is omitted, and the second is *akhbaraha*: i.e., it relates to the creation its news.

﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾ is connected to *tuhaddithu*. It is permissible that it be connected to *akhbaraha* itself. It was said that the *ba'* is extra, and that *anna* and what is within its scope is a substitution for *akhbaraha*. It was said that the *ba'* is causal: i.e., because of Allah's inspiring it.

al-Farra' said: it relates its news by the revelation of Allah and His permission to it. The *lam* in *awha laha* has the meaning of *ila* ("to"), and it was only given precedence over *ila* to match the rhyme (fawasil). The Arabs place the *lam* of attribution where *ila* would be; so said Abu ʿUbaydah.

It was said that *awha* is transitive with *lam* at times and with *ila* at other times. It was said that the *lam* retains its own function of indicating cause, and the one to whom it is inspired is omitted, namely the angels, and the meaning is: he inspired the angels for the sake of the earth, i.e., for the sake of what they do upon it. The first (view) is preferable.

﴿On that day people will issue forth in scattered groups﴾. The adverbial phrase (al-zarf) is either a substitution for *yawma'idhin* of the preceding verse, or it is in the accusative governed by an implied "udhkur" (remember), or it is in the accusative governed by what follows it. The meaning: on the day when what has been mentioned occurs, people will come forth from their graves to the place of reckoning in scattered groups, i.e., dispersed. *Al-sadr* means return, the opposite of arrival (wurud). It was said: they will go forth from the place of reckoning to Paradise or the Fire. *Ashtatan* is in the accusative as a state (hal). The meaning: some of them are secure and some are fearful; some have the color of the people of Paradise, which is whiteness, and some have the color of the people of the Fire, which is blackness; some turn toward the right and some toward the left, along with their dispersal in religions and their differing in deeds.

﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾ is connected to *yasdur*. It was said that there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it: i.e., "She relates her news, because your Lord has inspired her, that they may be shown their deeds, on that day people will issue forth in scattered groups."

al-Jumhur read *liyurau* in the passive voice, from sight (ru'yat al-basar): i.e., that Allah may show them their deeds.

al-Hasan, al-A'raj, Qatadah, Hammad ibn Salamah, Nasr ibn ʿAsim, and Talhah ibn Musarrif read it in the active voice, and this reading is reported from Nafi'. The meaning: that they may see the recompense of their deeds.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾, meaning the weight of an ant, which is the smallest of ants.

Muqatil said: "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it" on the Day of Resurrection in his book, and he will rejoice in it.

Likewise, whoever does an atom's weight of evil in this world ﴿will see it﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, and it will grieve him. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight﴾ [al-Nisa': 40].

Some of the linguists said: *al-dharrah* is when a man strikes the ground with his hand and whatever dust clings to it is the *dharrah*. It was said: *al-dharr* is what is seen in the rays of the sun as floating particles. The first is preferable. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*From the restrained-gazed (mares), if a small mite crept on the saddle-cloth of their (hooves) it would leave a mark.*

The first *min* refers to the fortunate, and the second *min* refers to the wretched.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "So whoever does an atom's weight of good from a disbeliever will see its reward in this world, in his self, his wealth, his family, and his children, until he leaves the world, and he will have no good with Allah. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil from a believer will see its punishment in this world, in his wealth, his self, his family, and his children, until he leaves the world, and he will have no evil with Allah." The first view is preferable.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning two men: one of them, when a beggar came to him, considered it too much to give him a date or a morsel; and the other would treat a small sin lightly and say: "Allah only threatened the Fire against the disbelievers."

al-Jumhur read *yarahu* in both places with a damma on the ha' when connected, and with sukun when pausing. Hisham read it with sukun both in connection and in pause. Abu Hayyan transmitted from Hisham and Abu Bakr the sukun, and from Abu ʿAmr the damma prolonged; the rest of the seven read with prolonging the first and sukun on the second. There is scrutiny in this transmission, and the correct is what we have mentioned.

al-Jumhur read *yarahu* as active in both places.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Hasan, al-Husayn son of ʿAli, Zayd ibn ʿAli, Abu Haywah, ʿAsim, al-Kisa'i in one narration from them, al-Jahdari, al-Sulami, and ʿIsa read it in the passive in both places: i.e., Allah shows it to him.

ʿIkrimah read *yarahu* on the supposition that *man* is a relative pronoun, or on the presumption of the jussive by dropping the presumed vowel of the verb.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding ﴿When the earth is shaken with its shaking﴾: he said: it was moved from its bottom. ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾: he said: the dead. ﴿And man says: What is wrong with it?﴾: he said: the disbeliever says, "What is wrong with it?" ﴿On that day it will relate its news﴾: he said: her Lord said to her, "Speak." ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾: he said: He inspired it. ﴿On that day people will issue forth in scattered groups﴾: he said: from every direction, from here and from here.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾: he said: the treasures and the dead.

Muslim and at-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The earth will throw out the fruits of its liver, like pillars of gold and silver. The killer will come and say: 'For this I killed.' The one who severed ties of kinship will come and say: 'For this I severed my kinship.' The thief will come and say: 'For this my hand was cut off.' Then they will leave it and take nothing from it."

Ahmad, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, at-Tirmidhi (who graded it sound), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Abu Hurairah who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿On that day it will relate its news﴾ and said: 'Do you know what its news is?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Its news is that it will bear witness against every male and female servant regarding what they did upon its back: it will say, "He did such and such." That is its news.'"

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the earth will come on the Day of Resurrection with every deed that was done upon its back," and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿When the earth is shaken with its shaking﴾ until he reached ﴿On that day it will relate its news﴾.

Al-Tabarani narrated from Rabi'ah al-Kharashi that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be careful of the earth, for it is your mother, and there is no one who acts upon it with good or evil except that it will inform of it."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, al-Hakim in his History, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from Anas who said: "While Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was eating with the Prophet (ﷺ), there was revealed to him ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ and ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾ Abu Bakr raised his hand and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I see that I have done an atom's weight of evil.' He said: 'O Abu Bakr, have you seen what you see in this world of what you dislike? It is by atoms' weights of evil; and there is stored up for you atoms' weights of good, until you are paid them in full on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Asma, who said: "While Abu Bakr was eating lunch with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. Abu Bakr stopped eating and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we have done no evil without seeing it [its consequence]?' He said, 'Do you not see what you dislike? That is what you are repaid for [in this world]. And good is deferred for its people in the Hereafter.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab (al-Iman) narrated from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: "The verse ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake﴾ (p-1647) was revealed, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was sitting and wept. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, 'What makes you weep, O Abu Bakr?' He said, 'This surah makes me weep.' He said, 'If you did not sin and commit wrongs so that Allah forgave you, Allah would create a people who sin and commit wrongs, and He would forgive them.'"

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Horses are for three [kinds of people]: for one man they are a reward, for one man they are a shield, and for one man they are a burden," and the hadith [continues]. He was asked about donkeys, and he said: "Nothing was revealed to me concerning them except this comprehensive and unique verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾."

*From the restrained-gazed (mares), if a small mite crept on the saddle-cloth of their (hooves) it would leave a mark.*

The first *min* refers to the fortunate, and the second *min* refers to the wretched.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "So whoever does an atom's weight of good from a disbeliever will see its reward in this world, in his self, his wealth, his family, and his children, until he leaves the world, and he will have no good with Allah. The first view is preferable.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning two men: one of them, when a beggar came to him, considered it too much to give him a date or a morsel; and the other would treat a small sin lightly and say: "Allah only threatened the Fire against the disbelievers."

It is Madani according to the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah, and Makki according to the view of Ibn Masʿud, ʿAta', and Jabir.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "It was revealed at Madinah: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its (final) shaking﴾."

He said: 'Recite three of the ones with the letter ra' (dhawat al-ra').' The man said: 'My age has grown old, my heart has become hard, and my tongue has become thick.' He said: 'Recite three of the ones with ha-mim (dhawat ha-mim).' He said the same as his first statement. He said: 'Recite three of the glorifying surahs (al-musabbihat).' He said the same as his first statement, and said: 'But teach me, O Messenger of Allah, a comprehensive surah.' So he taught him ﴿When the earth is shaken with its shaking﴾ until he finished it. The man said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I will not add to it.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'He has succeeded, the little man (al-Ruwayjil) has succeeded, the little man has succeeded.'"

At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾ is credited with half of the Qur'an, whoever recites ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ is credited with a third of the Qur'an, and whoever recites ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ is credited with a quarter of the Qur'an."

At-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Durays, Muhammad ibn Nasr, al-Hakim (who graded it sound), and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "*When it is shaken* equals half of the Qur'an, ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ equals a third of the Qur'an, and ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ equals a quarter of the Qur'an."

At-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib; we do not know it except through the hadith of Yaman ibn al-Mughirah."

At-Tirmidhi narrated from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man among his companions: "Have you married, so-and-so?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, and I do not have what I could marry with." He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a third of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the help of Allah comes and the victory﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an." He said: "Do you not have ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾?" He said: "Yes." He said: "It is a quarter of the Qur'an. Marry!"

At-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurairah: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever recites *When it is shaken* in a night, he will have the reward of half of the Qur'an.'"

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its shaking﴾, meaning when it is moved with a violent movement. The answer of the conditional is "it will relate" (tuhaddithu). The intended meaning is that it is moved at the establishment of the Hour, for it will convulse until everything upon it is shattered.

Mujahid said: It is the first blast, due to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 6–7]. The verbal noun is mentioned for emphasis, then it is attributed to the earth; it is a verbal noun attributed to its agent. The meaning: its particular shaking which it deserves and which its body and immensity require.

al-Jumhur read *zilzalaha* with a kasra on the zay, while al-Jahdari and ʿIsa read it with a fatha. Both are verbal nouns with the same meaning. It was said that the kasra form is a verbal noun and the fatha form is a noun (ism).

al-Qurtubi said: *al-zalzal* with a fatha is a verbal noun like *al-waswas* and *al-qalqal*.

﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾, meaning what is within its interior of the dead and the hidden treasures. *Al-athqal* is the plural of *thiql*. Abu ʿUbaydah and al-Akhfash said: if the dead person is in the belly of the earth, he is a burden to it; and if he is above it, he is a burden upon it.

Mujahid said: "Its burdens" are its dead, which it brings forth at the second blast. It has been said that mankind and jinn are called *al-thaqalan* (the two burdens). The mention of "the earth" in the place of a pronoun is to increase emphasis.

﴿And man says: What is wrong with it?﴾, meaning each individual of mankind says: What has happened to it that it is shaken?, because of what overwhelms him of its affair and what dazzles him of its calamity. It was said that the intended "man" is the disbeliever. His saying "what is wrong with it" is a subject and predicate, and it carries the sense of wonder: i.e., what is the matter with it, or for what reason has it been shaken and brought forth its burdens?

His saying: *yawma'idhin* is a substitution (badal) for *idha*, and the governing element for both is His saying: ﴿it will relate its news﴾. It is permissible that the governing element of *idha* is omitted and the governing element of *yawma'idhin* is "it will relate." The meaning: on the day when it is shaken and brings forth, it will inform with its news and relate to them what was done upon it of good and evil, either by the tongue of its state, where it indicates that clearly, or by the tongue of speech, by Allah, glorified is He, making it speak.

It was said that this is connected to His saying: ﴿And man says: What is wrong with it?﴾, meaning: he said, "What is wrong with it," being amazed at that, ﴿it relates its news﴾. Yahya ibn Salam said: it relates its news by what it brought forth of its burdens. It was said: it relates the establishment of the Hour and that it has come and that the world has ended.

Ibn Jarir said: it makes clear its news by the quaking, the earthquake, and the bringing forth of the dead. The first object of *tuhaddithu* is omitted, and the second is *akhbaraha*: i.e., it relates to the creation its news.

﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾ is connected to *tuhaddithu*. It is permissible that it be connected to *akhbaraha* itself. It was said that the *ba'* is extra, and that *anna* and what is within its scope is a substitution for *akhbaraha*. It was said that the *ba'* is causal: i.e., because of Allah's inspiring it.

al-Farra' said: it relates its news by the revelation of Allah and His permission to it. The *lam* in *awha laha* has the meaning of *ila* ("to"), and it was only given precedence over *ila* to match the rhyme (fawasil). The Arabs place the *lam* of attribution where *ila* would be; so said Abu ʿUbaydah.

It was said that *awha* is transitive with *lam* at times and with *ila* at other times. It was said that the *lam* retains its own function of indicating cause, and the one to whom it is inspired is omitted, namely the angels, and the meaning is: he inspired the angels for the sake of the earth, i.e., for the sake of what they do upon it. The first (view) is preferable.

﴿On that day people will issue forth in scattered groups﴾. The adverbial phrase (al-zarf) is either a substitution for *yawma'idhin* of the preceding verse, or it is in the accusative governed by an implied "udhkur" (remember), or it is in the accusative governed by what follows it. The meaning: on the day when what has been mentioned occurs, people will come forth from their graves to the place of reckoning in scattered groups, i.e., dispersed. *Al-sadr* means return, the opposite of arrival (wurud). It was said: they will go forth from the place of reckoning to Paradise or the Fire. *Ashtatan* is in the accusative as a state (hal). The meaning: some of them are secure and some are fearful; some have the color of the people of Paradise, which is whiteness, and some have the color of the people of the Fire, which is blackness; some turn toward the right and some toward the left, along with their dispersal in religions and their differing in deeds.

﴿That they may be shown their deeds﴾ is connected to *yasdur*. It was said that there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it: i.e., "She relates her news, because your Lord has inspired her, that they may be shown their deeds, on that day people will issue forth in scattered groups."
